title: Office — frame, File tab, and two wording checks

steps.headline: Toolbar, side strips and bottom bar now form one frame around the sheet: no gap at the left, no line under the header.
steps.changed: Ribbon, left/right icon strips and the bottom bar are one panel colour with no lines between them. The sheet sits in a single rounded, outlined window inside that frame, and the whole editor is a rounded card on the Office page.
steps.notice: The document area is clearly framed; the toolbar no longer floats as a separate card.
steps.risk: The editor's outer edge sits a few pixels in from the window edge, so the sheet is slightly narrower.

steps.headline: Word gets the same frame.
steps.changed: Same one-piece frame and rounded document window as Excel.
steps.notice: Word, Excel and PowerPoint now look the same around the edges.

steps.headline: PowerPoint gets the same frame.
steps.changed: Same frame; the slide list and the slide sit inside the same rounded window.

steps.headline: The File tab's pages sit on YouCoded cards, inside the same frame.
steps.changed: The File menu list stays on the frame's panel colour; its page (Info here) sits in the rounded document window, with the content on a card.
steps.notice: The File tab no longer looks like a different program, and it is clearly separate from the tab row and the selected menu item.
steps.risk: The document's own thumbnail isn't shown on the Info page (the editor doesn't make one offline).

steps.headline: Export (Save As) and Advanced Settings pages use the same cards.
steps.changed: Format choices and settings sit on cards in the same rounded window.
steps.notice: Every File page looks the same.

steps.path: A Word document with a side panel open (paragraph settings)
steps.headline: Side panels open inside the frame, joined to the strip they open from.
steps.changed: The panel uses the frame colour and joins the icon strip; the document window shrinks beside it.
steps.notice: No floating panel edges or double borders.

steps.path: A Word document → Home → styles gallery
steps.headline: The clean gallery look from the spreadsheet now applies to Word and PowerPoint too.
steps.changed: Square style tiles with one outline; the same menu edges and shadows as Excel.
steps.notice: What you approved for Excel now holds in all three editors.

steps.path: The status line at the top right of the Office page, after File → Save As
steps.headline: After a Save As, the status line says: "Saved a copy as Budget.pdf in Documents."
steps.changed: Stated, not asked: Save As writes a separate copy and you keep editing the original. If you pick the file you're editing, it says "That's the file you're editing. Choose another name."
steps.notice: You always know where the copy went and that your open document didn't change.

steps.path: The status line at the top right of the Office page, while editing a large document
steps.headline: While changes wait to be saved, should the status line say "Edited" instead of "Saving…"?
steps.today: Big documents now autosave up to 20 seconds after your last change (so typing isn't interrupted). During that wait the status line already says "Saving…".
steps.problem: "Saving…" for 20 seconds looks like the save is stuck, even though nothing is wrong.
steps.proposal: Show "Edited" while waiting, "Saving…" only while the save actually runs, then "Saved".

options.label: Keep "Saving…"
cons: Looks stuck on big documents for up to 20 seconds.
